content.user_title: Optimize Resumes for ATS Keyword Matching
content.value_statement: Resume formatting and missing job keywords can make relevant experience harder to identify. This skill guides formatting reviews, keyword comparisons, and targeted resume edits.
actual_capabilities: Review available resume content against a checklist for file format, layout, section headings, and contact information.
Extract technical skills, soft skills, and industry terms from supplied job descriptions.
Compare keywords using exact phrases, variations, frequency, and placement within resume sections.
Estimate keyword coverage using matched keywords divided by required keywords.
Suggest keyword placement and before-and-after wording for summaries, skills, and experience bullets.
Structure recommendations into a report covering formatting issues, keyword gaps, and estimated improvements.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not a bundled document parser, ATS simulator, or employer-system integration.
Keyword coverage estimates do not predict actual ATS decisions, interviews, or hiring outcomes.
Reliable keyword comparison requires both a resume and a target job description.
File extraction and layout inspection depend on host tools; suggested achievements and metrics require user verification.

use_cases.title: Tailor a graduate resume
use_cases.description: Match coursework, projects, and internships to entry-level job requirements while improving section headings and keyword placement.

use_cases.title: Present transferable experience
use_cases.description: Identify target-industry terminology that accurately describes existing skills and prepare a focused resume version.

use_cases.title: Organize client resume feedback
use_cases.description: Prepare structured formatting reviews and keyword-gap reports for clients applying to specific roles.

prompt_templates.title: Review basic resume structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this resume for standard headings, contact placement, and formatting risks: [resume]. Separate observable issues from layout checks requiring the original file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a resume before selecting a target role.

prompt_templates.title: Compare job keywords
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my resume [resume] with this job description [job description]. List matched and missing keywords, phrase variations, and an estimated keyword coverage score.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess alignment with one job posting.

prompt_templates.title: Revise targeted sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [resume] and [job description] to suggest summary, skills, and experience edits. Preserve facts, avoid keyword stuffing, and ask before adding unsupported qualifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: turn keyword analysis into specific wording changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an evidence-based report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ATS compatibility report from [resume] and [job description]. Show required keywords, evidence locations, matching assumptions, formatting uncertainties, and prioritized edits. Recalculate keyword coverage after proposed edits, marking unverified additions separately. Do not claim testing in an ATS unless a test actually occurred.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: produce a traceable review with transparent scoring and verification limits.

output_examples.input: A posting requires Python, SQL, Excel, and Tableau. The supplied resume includes Python, SQL, and Excel.
output: Estimated keyword coverage: 75%, based on three of four required terms.
Matched terms: Python, SQL, and Excel.
Missing term: Tableau. Add it only if supported by actual experience.
This estimate is not an employer ATS score.

output_examples.input: A resume uses two columns, places contact details in a header, and labels work history as My Journey.
output: Use a single-column layout to simplify reading order.
Move contact details into the document body.
Rename My Journey to Professional Experience.
Verify text extraction from the final document using available tools.

best_practices: Provide a current resume and the complete target job description; remove personal details that are unnecessary for review.
Verify every suggested skill, achievement, and metric before including it in an application.
Review the final document for readable formatting and distinguish estimated keyword coverage from actual ATS testing.
anti_patterns: Adding skills, credentials, or numerical achievements solely because a job description mentions them.
Repeating keywords excessively or replacing clear experience descriptions with disconnected keyword lists.
Treating an estimated match percentage as a guaranteed screening result or interview prediction.

faq.question: Which assistants support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Document inspection capabilities depend on the host environment and available tools.

faq.question: What should I provide for a review?
faq.answer: Provide your resume and the target job description. Resume text supports keyword analysis; the original document helps when layout inspection tools are available.

faq.question: Does the match score represent an employer ATS score?
faq.answer: No. It estimates keyword coverage using matched terms divided by required terms. Employers may use different parsing, ranking, and screening rules.

faq.question: Can it directly test PDF and DOCX files?
faq.answer: The skill recommends text-based PDF or DOCX files but includes no parser. Direct inspection requires compatible tools in your assistant environment.

faq.question: Does the skill upload my resume to an external service?
faq.answer: No upload destination or network integration is specified in the reviewed file. Your assistant provider still governs data handling for submitted resumes.

faq.question: What should I do with missing keywords?
faq.answer: Add missing terms only when they accurately describe your experience. Treat unsupported terms as qualification gaps, not instructions to invent experience.
